content.title: 14.6 Amyloidosis
content.epidemiology_summary: Cardiac amyloidosis (CA) is underdiagnosed. The two most prevalent forms are light chain immunoglobulin (AL) and transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis. ATTR includes wild-type (>90% of ATTR cases) and hereditary/variant (<10%). It is estimated that 6–16% of patients with unexplained LVH or HFpEF at hospitalization or severe aortic stenosis undergoing valve replacement, aged >65 years, may have wild-type TTR-CA.
diagnosis_criteria: Age >65 years and heart failure with LV wall thickness >12 mm on echocardiography are major criteria for suspicion of CA.
Criteria for suspicion and confirmation include multimodality imaging and extracardiac biopsy or endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) when haematological tests are abnormal.

imaging_tests.nuclear_scintigraphy: Technetium-labelled 99mTc-PYP, DPD or HMDP planar and SPECT imaging has high specificity and positive predictive value for TTR-CA (up to 100% reported).
imaging_tests.CMR: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) has sensitivity ~85% and specificity ~92% for CA.
imaging_tests.note: A biopsy may not be needed when scintigraphy with SPECT shows grade 2–3 positivity in appropriate context.

content.biopsy_and_genetic_testing: Endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) is the gold standard for diagnosis of TTR-CA with nearly 100% sensitivity and specificity if specimens are collected from >4 sites and tested with Congo red staining. The hereditary form should be excluded by genetic testing.
content.references_note: The guideline references multiple studies and tables (e.g., Table 35, Supplementary Table 25, Figure 21) for criteria and diagnostic algorithms.

genes.context: Transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis is one of the two most prevalent forms of cardiac amyloidosis; text refers to wild-type (>90%) and hereditary/variant (<10%) ATTR, mentions wtTTR-CA, and discusses positive predictive value of scintigraphy for TTR-CA and the need to exclude hereditary form by genetic testing.
